description: What the modding tools' Lua editor shows about the script API: "functions" maps a name the scripts can call to its signature (arguments in call order, [optional], -> results) and a one-line description. Units: positions and lengths are Q12 (4096 = 1 m), angles Q12 (4096 = a full turn), times Q12 seconds, unless the description says otherwise. A character is its slot number (0 the player). The names are checked against the running game with tools/scripts/lua_api_docs.py; a mod describes the API it adds in its own tools/lua_api.json.

Works from a map event and from any other script (a mod's main.lua, a coroutine): there it starts once no map event runs.

sh.save.set_clear_game_count.description: Sets: the count of finished games kept in the save.

sh.save.set_clear_game_endings.description: Sets: the endings seen, as kept in the save.

sh.save.set_current_ending_flags.description: Sets: the ending flags of this playthrough.

sh.save.set_game_difficulty.description: Sets the difficulty kept in the save.

sh.save.set_location_id.description: Sets: the location number kept in the save.

sh.save.set_map_idx.description: Sets the map number kept in the save.

sh.save.set_next_fear_mode.description: Sets: bit 0 of the mode bits of the save: a Next Fear game.

sh.savegame_get.description: A field of the save: "map_idx", "paper_map_idx" (a page name), "item_toggle_flags".

sh.savegame_set.description: Writes a field of the save (see savegame_get).

sh.screen.bg_gamma.description: The gamma the background picture is drawn with.

sh.screen.bg_transition.description: Cross-fades between two pictures (item_inspection_img, bg_texture_img or a map variable).

sh.screen.credits_roll_music_started.description: True when the music of the staff roll has started.

sh.screen.credits_roll_start.description: Starts the staff roll for an ending.

sh.screen.fade_status.description: The status word of the screen fade.

sh.screen.pickup_animate.description: Turns the model of a picked-up item towards the camera; true when it faces it.

sh.screen.set_bg_gamma.description: Sets: the gamma the background picture is drawn with.

sh.screen.set_fade_status.description: Sets: the status word of the screen fade.

sh.screen_fade_finished.description: True when the screen fade has finished.

sh.screen_fade_reset_timestep.description: Puts the screen fade's speed back to its default.

sh.screen_fade_timestep_set.description: Sets the screen fade's time step.

sh.sd_call.description: Sends a command number to the sound driver.

sh.sd_play_sfx.description: Plays a sound with a stereo balance and a volume.

sh.selection_silent.description: Makes the next "yes" of a choice silent.

sh.session.get.description: An integer kept by name for the life of the process (not saved, survives map changes).

sh.session.set.description: Stores an integer by name for the life of the process.

sh.sfx.description: Plays a sound by registry name or number.

sh.sfx_3d.description: Plays a sound at the point of the active map event.

sh.sfx_3d_at.description: Plays a sound at a position in the world.

sh.sfx_falloff_pitch_play.signature: sh.sfx_falloff_pitch_play(sound, x, y, z[, vol[, falloff[, pitch]]])
sh.sfx_falloff_pitch_play.description: Plays a sound at a position with a distance falloff and a pitch.

sh.sfx_flags_pitch_play.signature: sh.sfx_flags_pitch_play(sound, x, y, z, vol, flags, pitch)

sh.sfx_flags_play.signature: sh.sfx_flags_play(sound, x, y, z[, vol[, flags]])
sh.sfx_flags_play.description: Plays a sound at a position with flags: 1 mono, 2 no distance attenuation, 4 update attributes.

sh.sfx_pitch_play.signature: sh.sfx_pitch_play(sound, x, y, z[, vol[, pitch]])
sh.sfx_pitch_play.description: Plays a sound at a position with a pitch.

sh.sound.exists.description: True when the registry has the sound.

sh.sound.swap.description: While set, every call of the game's sound (a registry name or number) plays a file of the active mods instead (a path inside the mod folder, "sounds/mymod/hiss.wav" or a .opus file; volume 1, pitch 0 semitones and loop true by default); the sound stops first if it plays. sh.sound.swap(sound) ends it, sh.sound.swap() ends every one. Not saved: set it again after a load (a map.load hook). false when no active mod has the file. Example: sh.sound.swap("radio_static_loop", "sounds/mymod/static.wav", {volume = 0.9}).

sh.sound.id.description: The number of a sound by registry name; an unknown name is an error.

sh.sound.music_channels.description: The sound driver's count of busy music channels; 0 when the track stopped.

sh.sound.music_layer_volume_set.description: Sets the driver's volume of one music layer (0..255) at once.

sh.sound.name.description: The registry name of a sound number.

sh.sound.play_3d.description: Plays a sound at a position in the world.

sh.sound.play_3d_falloff.signature: sh.sound.play_3d_falloff(sfx, x, y, z, vol, falloff, pitch)
sh.sound.play_3d_falloff.description: Plays a sound at a position with a distance falloff and a pitch.

sh.sound.sfx_mix_update.signature: sh.sound.sfx_mix_update(sfx, x, y, z, volume, range, mode)
sh.sound.sfx_mix_update.description: The positional music mix (the park's music box): pan and volume from the player's distance to the point; range is the distance it is heard within.

sh.spawn.description: Starts fn as a coroutine the host steps every tick (up to 256 alive); inside it use wait(), wait_frames() and wait_until().

sh.state_set.description: The next system state; 0 returns to gameplay and ends the handler.

sh.state_timer_get.description: The state's timer (the cross-fade alpha, Q12 0..1).

sh.take_item.description: Removes n (default 1) of an item from the inventory.

sh.text.description: The text of a key in the current language, and whether the key exists.

sh.ui.fade.description: Starts a screen fade: in (true) or out, to white when white is true.

sh.ui.fade_done.description: True when the screen fade has finished.

sh.ui.msg_draw.description: Draws a message for this tick: 0 still showing, -1 finished, 1..3 the chosen answer. Call once a tick; msg is a text key or number (a message of the loaded map, or of text/<lang>/messages.json on any map).

sh.vc_cam_target.description: Sets the position the camera moves to (Q12).

sh.vc_stereo_balance.description: The stereo balance of a world point as the camera hears it.

sh.vc_watch_target.description: Sets the point the camera watches (Q12).

sh.vec.get.description: Scratch vector i (0..15); scripts pass it to the API as "vec:i".

sh.vec.set.description: Sets scratch vector i (0..15), referenced as "vec:i".

sh.vec.short_set.description: Sets 16-bit scratch vector i, referenced as "svec:i".

sh.world.cell.description: The map cell of a point.

sh.world.chunk_set.description: Places a world chunk in a cell; file is the number of an IPD file (sh.file_number("BG/X.IPD")).

sh.world.darkness_at.description: How dark a point of the world is, 0..255.

sh.world.effect_slot_alloc.description: Takes a map effect slot for an effect type; -1 when none is free.

sh.world.effect_slot_get.description: Reads a field of a map effect slot: x, z, y, type, variant, s32_0..1, s16_0..3, u16_0..3, u8_0..7.

sh.world.effect_slot_set.description: Writes a field of a map effect slot; the write keeps the field's width.

sh.world.effects_flags.description: The flags of the environment preset: bit 0 a dark setting, bit 1 the flashlight matters.

sh.world.effects_track.description: The map effects blend from preset0 to preset1 as the value of tracked cell (0..3) goes from min to max.

sh.world.effects_track_set.description: Sets the value of a tracked cell of the map effects blend.

sh.world.fog_floor_request.description: Raises the live fog to at least the stock level for this frame.

sh.world.ground_height.description: The height of the ground under a point.

sh.world.light_flags.description: The flag byte of the current environment preset: bit 0 the dark set-up, bit 1 an area where the flashlight matters.

sh.world.nearest_walkable.signature: sh.world.nearest_walkable(x, z[, radius[, from_x, from_z]]) -> x, z, y
sh.world.nearest_walkable.description: The nearest point with ground within radius (default 2 m, at most 16 m); nil when there is none.

sh.world.object_add.description: Adds a world object of the map by name to this frame's objects.

sh.world.object_draw.signature: sh.world.object_draw(name, x, y, z, rx, ry, rz)
sh.world.object_draw.description: Draws a "script" world object once more this tick at another place.

sh.world.object_model_name_set.description: Gives a world object another model.

sh.world.pickup_create.signature: sh.world.pickup_create{item, x, y, z, rot, id, flag, count, message, model, units} -> id or nil, err
sh.world.pickup_create.description: Puts a real pickup on the loaded map; flag (from the mod's flags.json) marks it taken. Call it at every map load. model is a world model name of the map (8 characters at most), the item's world_model by default, or false: nothing is drawn for it (the mod shows the thing as a world object of its own model) and it is still taken up there. message is the key of the prompt: a message of the map or of text/<lang>/messages.json.

sh.world.mark.description: A place of the script's story (a trigger zone of its own, a save point, a door it shuts, a monster waiting to come) that the modding tools' overlay draws: x, z and the radius r in metres, a label and a free kind text. Nothing in the game sees it. Gone at a map change: mark the places again in a map.load hook. Example: sh.world.mark("lever", {x = 12.5, z = -3.0, r = 1.5, label = "the lever", kind = "action"}).

sh.world.message.description: Shows a message (its text key or number) as soon as Harry is free, the world stopped, like the map's own message events. The key is a message of the loaded map (a mod adds one with a text file that has "map") or a message of no map from text/<lang>/messages.json, which every map can show.

sh.world.pickup_remove.description: Removes a pickup the script created.

sh.world.pickup_take.description: Opens the prompt of a pickup the script created as if the player had taken it up there, wherever the player stands (once no map event runs and the player is free): the end of a scene can hand the player its item with the game's own question. false when the map has no such pickup. Example: sh.world.pickup_create{item = "Key", x = 1.5, z = 2.0, id = "key", flag = "key_taken", message = "take_key", model = false}; sh.world.pickup_take("key").

sh.world.pickups.description: The script pickups of the map: {id, owner, item, model, flag, count, message, x, y, z, rot, taken}.

sh.world.unmark.description: Removes one of the script's marks (sh.world.mark), or every one of them without an id; true when one went.

sh.world.ray.signature: sh.world.ray(fx, fy, fz, tx, ty, tz[, mode[, exclude_slot]])
sh.world.ray.description: Casts a ray; mode is "solid", "chara", "sight" or "probe"; slot is -1 when it hit geometry.

sh.world.ray_surface.signature: sh.world.ray_surface(x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1)
sh.world.ray_surface.description: Casts a ray against the collision surface.

sh.world.script_call.description: Calls a global function of the map's world_objects.lua.

sh.world.speed_zone.description: The speed zone of a point: 0 slow, 1 normal, 2 fast.

sh.world.walkable.signature: sh.world.walkable(x, z[, from_x, from_z]) -> ok, ground_y
sh.world.walkable.description: Whether the point has loaded ground; with from, also whether it can be walked to from there (height step and walls).

sh.world_object.model_set.description: Changes the model of a world object (a name of up to 8 characters).

sh.world_object.position_get.description: The position of any world object of the map.

sh.world_object.position_set.description: Moves a world object of world_objects.json (one with "script": true), Q12.

sh.world_object.rotation_get.description: The rotation of any world object of the map.

sh.world_object.rotation_set.description: Turns a world object, Q12 angles kept in 16 bits.

sh.world_object.visible_set.description: Shows a world object always (true), never (false) or as the map data says (nil).

sh.world_object_add.description: Adds a world object of the map by name to this frame's objects.

sh.world_objects.call.description: Calls a global function of the map's world_objects.lua from the events script.

sh.xa_preload.description: Prepares a streamed voice line for playing.

string.byte.description: The byte values of characters of s.

string.char.description: A string of the given byte values.

string.find.signature: string.find(s, pattern[, init[, plain]]) -> start, end

string.gmatch.description: Iterates over the matches of a pattern.

string.gsub.signature: string.gsub(s, pattern, repl[, n]) -> string, count
string.gsub.description: Replaces the matches of a pattern.

string.len.description: The length of s in bytes.

string.match.description: The captures of the first match of a pattern.

string.sub.description: The part of s from i to j.

table.concat.description: Joins the strings of a list.

table.insert.description: Inserts a value at pos (default the end).

table.remove.description: Removes and returns the element at pos (default the last).

table.unpack.description: The elements of a list as separate values.

tonumber.description: Converts a string to a number; nil when it is not one.

tostring.description: Converts a value to a string.

type.description: The type of a value as a string.

wait.description: In a coroutine: waits a time in logic ticks (30 per second).

wait_fade.description: In a coroutine: waits until the screen fade has finished.

wait_frames.description: In a coroutine: waits n ticks.

wait_until.description: In a coroutine: waits until fn() returns true.

sh.mods.import_can.description: Menu scripts: whether the system has a dialog to pick a mod "folder" or "zip".

sh.mods.import_clear.description: Menu scripts: forgets the scanned pick and the last import's report.

sh.mods.import_found.description: Menu scripts: the mods found in the pick, each with id, name, version, status (new, update, same, older, invalid), reason, notes ({kind, detail, need, have}: the parts of ui.mods.import.note.<kind>) and selected.

sh.mods.import_last.description: Menu scripts: the last import's {added, replaced} ids or nil, and its error ("" none).

sh.mods.import_pick.description: Menu scripts: opens the system's dialog for a mod "folder" or "zip"; the answer arrives later through import_poll.

sh.mods.import_poll.description: Menu scripts: every frame of the import page; scans a picked or dropped folder or .zip. state is idle, picking or ready.

sh.mods.import_run.description: Menu scripts: copies the chosen mods of the pick into the mods folder (all or nothing) and lists them; new mods are switched off.

sh.mods.import_scan.description: Menu scripts: scans a folder or .zip for mods now.

sh.mods.import_select.description: Menu scripts: chooses whether the found mod at index is imported; false for an invalid one.

sh.chara.model_override.description: Draws every character of a type (a name or a number) from another glb below convert/models/ ("mymod/LOOK.glb": a glb, or a manifest LOOK.model.json with "derive") bound to the type's skeleton; nil or no glb gives the type its own again. Not saved: set it again after a load.

sh.player.set_character.description: The player wears another character: the model and the inventory portrait of the key "as_player" in chara/<name>/character.json; nil gives back the player's own. Harry's controls, animations and sounds stay. Not saved: set it again after a load.

sh.assets.replace.description: While set, the game data path ("convert/textures/ITEM/HEROPIC2.png") is read from another file of the active mods (a path inside a mod folder); 0 when no active mod has the file. A picture or model already read is read again the next time the game loads it. Not saved.

sh.assets.restore.description: Ends the replacement of one path, or of every path without an argument; 1 when there was one.

sh.world.say.description: Shows a message (its text key or number) over play: the world goes on and the player can move; the confirm button advances it, its own waits end it. One at a time: a new one replaces it, a map event that starts drops it. The key is a message of the loaded map or, on any map, a message of text/<lang>/messages.json.

sh.world.saying.description: True while the message of sh.world.say still shows.

sh.world.hush.description: Ends the message of sh.world.say at once (a script that lets the player skip a line).

sh.event.run.description: Runs fn as the handler of an event of the script's own: from the next tick the game is in the event state (no other event starts, the world stands still while fn draws a paper map or holds the music) and calls fn() once a tick inside its update, where the event steppers (sh.event_step_get, sh.event_step_increment_after_fade, sh.event_msg, sh.event_waypoint_player) and the drawing of a map event (sh.map_screen_vertex_draw) work as in a handler of maps/<map>/events.lua. The event ends when fn returns true, or fails. It starts once no other event runs and the player is free (not frozen); false when an event of a script is asked for or runs already. A coroutine waits for it with sh.event.running(). Example: sh.event.run(function() if sh.event_step_get(0) == 0 then sh.event_step_increment_after_fade(2, true, 0, 0, false) return false end return true end).

sh.event.running.description: True while an event started with sh.event.run is asked for or runs.

sh.sound.fade.description: Moves a sound that plays a file (a "file" entry of sounds/*.json, or sh.sound.swap) to level of its volume (0 silent, 1 as it plays, up to 4) over seconds (0 or left out: at once), evenly in the mix, so there is no step in what is heard; with stop it ends when it gets there. A sound that is not playing keeps the level for its next play: sh.sound.fade(name, 0), sh.sound.play(name, 0, 0), sh.sound.fade(name, 1, 1.5) is a fade-in from silence. True when the sound was playing. The game's bank sounds are not changed. Example: sh.sound.fade("mymod:hum", 0, 2.0, true).
